The short version

A rich, spicy double-oak rye with distinctive texture and fruit. Independent reports also identify drying wood, bitterness and aromatic roughness, so darker oak does not automatically mean better execution.

Exact identity: Lot No. 40 Dark Oak, recurring NAS 100% rye, 48% ABV / 96 proof, 750 mL; second heavily charred-oak maturation.

Background and history

Selfbuilt’s November 26, 2020 review documents the Canadian introduction before wider distribution; producer shop publication in May 2021 is not the first release date.

A separate October 2022 issuer announcement documents U.S. introduction. Retailer copy assigning Dark Oak itself to 1998 confuses this extension with the parent brand.

For the shared historical context, read Canadian whisky, cross-border trade and the American market. The release chronology above distinguishes the current bottle from its brand’s earlier history.

Producer, grains, aging and finishing

Producer verifies new American-oak maturation followed by a second barrel charred to level four. Specialist reporting identifies a number-two initial char. NAS remains NAS; the finish duration and total component ages are not authenticated. Secondary NEW oak is not merely a re-char of the original barrel. Current producer pack confirms 48%.

Producer / source
Hiram Walker & Sons, Windsor, Ontario / Pernod Ricard; Corby Spirit & Wine brand stewardship
Grain / mash composition
100% rye. Matched technical accounts describe unmalted rye, column distillation then copper-pot distillation; no corn or barley percentages inferred.
Strength

Finishing
Second new-oak cask charred to level four after initial new-American-oak maturation; duration undisclosed.

Critical review synthesis

Selfbuilt · Selfbuilt’s Whisky Analysis

The bottle retains recognizable fruit and spice but adds substantial wood and heat. A medium, drying finish and rapid loss of subtlety with dilution limit its appeal.

Scope: November 26, 2020 exact 48% sample; spice preference and execution limits distinguished.

Bourbon Culture · Bourbon Culture

The reviewer enjoys weighted, nearly syrupy texture and unusual fruit/herbal layers, while noting bandage/cleaning-like aromas and a somewhat bitter woody ending.

Scope: 2023 exact Dark Oak bottle brought from Canada; sensory descriptors do not identify additives or contamination.

Published sample evidence, not first-person tasting or a representative survey. Reviewer disagreement and recipe-era limitations remain explicit; publisher grades are not mechanically converted.

No representative crowd consensus is claimed. Attributed individual tasting reports are not a survey of drinkers.

Quality and calibration

Quality 6.7 / 10. Good provisional Canadian all-rye execution. Developed fruit/spice and substantial body are supported, while wood dryness, bitterness and reported chemical-like aromas limit balance and cleanliness. Those descriptors are not evidence of laboratory contamination.

No defensible complete Canadian native 1/5/10 framework is established for this comparison group. Seven universal execution dimensions are assessed within Canadian Single Grain / 100% Rye; unrelated American bourbon and straight-rye endpoints are not imported.

Calibration mode: evidence_limited_provisional. Evidence-limited provisional; matched independent tasting with sample and era limitations

Serving recommendations

Neat

Try a small full-strength pour and allow time in the glass; the matched accounts disagree on some finish and cask effects.

Water / rocks

Add only a few drops at a time and compare texture. Several reviewers find too much dilution reduces definition.

Old Fashioned

Keep syrup restrained; a recurring core rye is the price comparison before mixing a limited bottle.

Manhattan / highball

Try a small serve with vermouth or soda, adjusting sweetness and dilution to the cask influence.

Serving suggestions are editorial starting points, grounded in documented strength and style; adjust to your taste.
